timing.label: Objection 1 (technical)
timing.question: A plugin is one more supply chain to secure. Why should I let it run in every session?

timing.label: Objection 2 (commercial)
timing.question: Why not just hand each brand team a playbook and skip the packaging?

problem.quote: Every brand team will run the same flash-sale release checklist

approach.quote: The kade-flash-sale plugin ships both procedures as skills

evidence.quote: The checker reports zero problems and it is installed for me only

next_step.quote: I need your sign-off before Organization scope

must_mention.point: One plugin ships both procedures as skills together with the freeze rule, the push guard hook, the reviewer subagent and the incident MCP
must_mention.evidence_quote: The kade-flash-sale plugin ships both procedures as skills, together with the freeze rule, the push guard hook, the release-checker subagent and the incident MCP declaration

must_mention.point: Repository installs follow the branch unless pinned to a SHA, uploads stay pinned to what was uploaded, and a skills-only repo needs no manifest
must_mention.evidence_quote: the repository install follows the branch unless we pin it to a SHA, and the upload stays pinned to what we uploaded

must_mention.point: A new uploaded revision replaces the whole bundle, so a partial zip removes every file it left out
must_mention.evidence_quote: the new revision replaces the whole bundle, so the partial zip removed six files

must_mention.point: The MCP credential is connected after install through a secret reference and never written into the plugin files
must_mention.evidence_quote: the credential is connected after install from Connect MCP. It is never written into the plugin files

must_mention.point: Engineers without edit rights can only propose; an admin approves the diff before the shared plugin changes
must_mention.evidence_quote: engineers without edit rights can only propose; an admin approves the diff before the shared plugin changes

sentences_to_rerecord: Credentials: the MCP token is a dollar-brace reference, and the credential is connected after install from Connect MCP.

accuracy.anchor: Five of five points, each tied to a file, scope or count. (anchors: 27–30 every point with a file or scope named; 15–20 three of five; under 10 one point)

structure.anchor: Outcome first in the framing; the update held all six headings in order; the ask has a date. (anchors: 22–25 all parts in order; 13–17 parts present but weak; under 8 problem only)

customer_relevance.anchor: Answered the reviewer's three questions: what runs, where it came from, who can change it; brand count and checklist lengths given. (anchors: 16–20 reviewer's questions answered with files, scopes and counts; 10–13 some; under 6 feature talk)

brevity_and_fluency.anchor: Every segment within 5 s of target; one filler in about eight and a half minutes. (anchors: 11–15 segments on target, under 1 filler/min; 6–8 two or more segments off; under 4 most segments off)

recovery.anchor: Both objections held acknowledge → boundary → evidence → offer; objection 2 carried checklist counts. (anchors: 7–10 acknowledge → boundary → evidence → offer held with numbers; 4–6 partial; under 3 no pattern)

stems: "What runs, in one line, is…" — open the update with the file count before the scopes.
"The token lives in…" — answer the interruption in one clause, then return to the heading.
"Per release that is…" — put a number on the skipped-step count you offered to measure.
previous_run_comparison: Second grading of the same transcript; total moved by -1 point(s) from run 1.
